title: A Visit to a Chinese Garden

pages.text: I visit a garden from China. I go in at a gate. That gate has no doors. Lots of water is what I see. Like a mirror, the water is smooth. Things show in the water. I am glad to see that water.
A huge rock is what I see. It looks strong to me. The rock will not move. The rock will not fall. Being strong now makes me glad too.
Trees are what I see. The trees stand tall. The trees give shade. The trees make me feel glad. I can rest under them. The day is sunny.
This garden in China looks beautiful. The garden feels peaceful. I will remember that garden. Water will make me remember it. Rocks will make me remember it. Trees will make me remember it.

What is it like up on the Moon? The Moon is full of craters. Rocks fly through space. The rocks hit the Moon. Each hit creates a crater.
Gravity on the Moon is less. It is less than gravity on Earth. People can jump high there. There is almost no air there. People cannot breathe there.

Some animal dads help only a little. These dads give no help at all. Other animal dads are great helpers. Which dads are the great helpers?

The rhea dad guards his chicks. He cares for his chicks. All the help comes from him alone. He does this for almost two years. The marmoset dad cleans off bugs. Those bugs sit in his babies' fur. He helps feed his babies. He carries his babies too.

The poison dart frog dad carries tadpoles. The tadpoles sit on his back. He helps the tadpoles reach water. The emperor penguin dad holds an egg. The egg is on his feet. He keeps the egg warm. All around him it is cold.

The jawfish dad keeps eggs inside his mouth. This keeps the eggs safe. They wait there until they are born. The jackal dad takes in food. He spits that food back up. His pups get the food from him. Yum! His pups grow strong with his help.
A pouch is on the seahorse dad. He holds thousands of eggs in it. He helps them grow in there. He helps them hatch in there. Their young get help from these dads too.

Brazil is my home. Many animals live here too. I am a maned wolf. I look like a red fox with long legs. A hairy mane rises along my back.
Anaconda. My home is Brazil. I am the heaviest snake in the world. Toucan. My home is Brazil. I am very colorful with my long bill. Some people keep me as a pet.
Poison dart frog. My home is Brazil. Many pretty colors are on my skin. Do not touch me. My poison can kill. Marmoset. My home is Brazil. I am one small monkey. My tail is long.
Giant anteater. My home is Brazil. My long tongue grabs insects to eat. Capybara. My home is Brazil. I am the largest rodent in the world.
Piranha. My home is Brazil. Watch out if you swim in the river. My teeth are sharp! All these animals are from Brazil. I am from Brazil too!
Birds fly in the sky. Where do they go? See this eastern bluebird. Some birds migrate to other places. They go for part of the year. Many birds migrate before winter. They go so they can survive.
An American robin migrates for winter fruit. In spring it returns for worms. In spring it returns for insects. A snow goose migrates with its flock. Its flock is V-shaped.
Night is when a Baltimore oriole migrates. It rests when day comes. The air grows too cold. A hummingbird migrates at that time.
See the red-tailed hawk. Often this hawk migrates alone. See the tree swallow. It migrates in a flock. Thousands of birds are in the flock.
See the yellow warbler. It crosses the water with no stop. See the European robin. Some birds migrate down a mountain. Some birds migrate for thousands of miles. These birds always come back.
A glassblower is what I am. Come see the bowl as I make it. It is a beautiful glass bowl. The glass stays in the oven. That oven gets very, very hot. The runny hot glass is like honey.

My long pipe gets a dip in hot glass. I use the table to roll my pipe. Rolling makes the glass smooth. Rolling makes the glass cool. I blow into the pipe. A bubble grows in the gooey glass. My breath is not too hard.
Other colors get added to the bowl. Now the bowl looks more beautiful. The pipe goes back into the oven. Inside the oven, the colors start to flow.
Shape comes from the tools I use. I spin the glass with all my speed. The bowl grows wider each time. It keeps getting wider.
Next I break that pipe away. I heat the glass one more time. This makes the glass smooth. The glass cools bit by bit. My beautiful glass bowl is made.
People make piñatas from paper. People use glue on the paper. Piñatas have lots of shapes. Piñatas have lots of sizes. Some of them look like animals.
Some piñatas are like shapes. Every piñata has treats inside.
Many people like piñatas at a party. People take turns at the party. A stick is what they swing. They aim it at the piñata. Breaking it open is what they try.
Hitting the piñata is not easy. Some players put a cover on their eyes. Then the player swings the stick. Some players get spun around first. Then that player swings the stick.
During the swings, some piñatas are moved. Everyone feels happy when it breaks. The piñata breaks open. Candy falls out of it. Prizes fall out of it.
Which colors will I pick for my paintings? For this one I pick primary colors. Red is a primary color. Yellow is a primary color. Blue is a primary color.

For this one I pick secondary colors. Orange is a secondary color. Green is a secondary color. Purple is a secondary color. For this one I pick warm colors. Red is a warm color. Orange is a warm color. Yellow is a warm color.
For this one I pick cool colors. Blue is a cool color. Green is a cool color. Purple is a cool color. For this one I pick shades. Shades come when black is added.
For this one I pick tints. Tints come when white is added. For this one I pick opposite colors. The color green is opposite red.
The color purple is opposite yellow too. The color blue is opposite orange too. Those opposite colors are complementary ones. Picking painting colors is easy with a color wheel.
Have you tried rock climbing? Climbing rocks is fun. You can climb with friends. You can climb with family.

Climbing rocks is fun. You can climb up the rocks. You can climb down the rocks. You can climb across the rocks. Climbing rocks is fun. You can climb on cliffs outside. You can climb on large boulders outside.
Climbing rocks is fun. Climbing walls are inside. You can climb on them. Stay safe on your climb. Always climb slowly. Always climb carefully.
Stay safe on your climb. Wear a helmet when you climb. The helmet keeps your head safe. Stay safe on your climb. Wear good shoes when you climb.
Stay safe on your climb. Use ropes when you climb. Ropes catch you if you fall. You get to the top. At the top, you feel strong. At the top, you feel brave.

This woman was brave. Her name was Harriet Tubman. The United States was where she lived. She lived long ago. The South was the place of her birth. Her birth was into slavery. A white family kept her enslaved. She was a Black girl.

Harriet Tubman had to work hard. She got no pay. People did not treat her well. An 1860 map shows slavery in the United States. North and South are marked on the map. The letters N, W, E, and S are marked too. Free states are marked. Slave states are marked. Areas open to slavery are marked. When she grew up, she escaped to the North. There she could live free.

Her wish was freedom for other enslaved people. Many trips took her back to the South. Her help let enslaved people escape. A trip back to the South was for her family. Her family did escape. A trip back to the South was for her friends. Her friends did escape.
Every South trip put her in danger. She was the one they wanted to catch. They wanted her enslaved once more. Punishing her was what they wanted. She had helped enslaved people escape.

Tubman took care each time. No one ever caught Tubman. New York City, New York, has a famous statue. That statue is the one on the left. Boston, Massachusetts, has a famous statue. That statue is the one on the right. A hero is the name for Harriet Tubman. Many enslaved people went free with her help.

What amazing insects these beetles are. A beetle has a head. A beetle has legs. Three main body parts are on a beetle. Other insects have those three parts too. Soft wings sit at the back. Hard wings sit at the front. The front wings are also thick. They protect the wing pair under them. Ladybugs are also called ladybirds. They are a very common beetle. Two pairs of wings show up on most beetles.
Every beetle has a hard skeleton. The skeleton is on the outside. It protects the beetle. Beetle kinds are many. Beetles have more kinds than any other living thing.

Beetles can make a home almost anywhere. A forest can be that home. A desert can be that home. The top beetle is a jewel beetle. It rests on a leaf. That leaf is in a jungle. The bottom beetle is a great diving beetle. It swims underwater. A jungle can be a beetle home. Water can be a beetle home. Around water can be a beetle home.

An egg comes first. A young beetle hatches from that egg. It sheds its skin as it grows. It sheds one or more times. A new shape comes after that. The shape protects it. During this time, it changes into an adult. Beetles go through several changes as they grow. Each change makes them look very different. A ground beetle is shown on top. It eats dead leaves. A burying beetle is shown on the bottom. It eats a dead squirrel. Beetles eat many kinds of food. Some eat dead plants. Some eat dead animals.

Dung beetles are on top. They work together. They roll animal waste into a ball. A red milkweed beetle is on the bottom. A milkweed plant is food for this beetle. Animal waste feeds some beetles. Plants feed some beetles. Other insects feed some beetles. These beetles are amazing insects.

I live in Australia. The country is large. Lots of open space is here. Many animals live here. I am a platypus. Rivers are my home. A beaver is the animal I look like. A duck’s bill is like my bill. My food is tasty bugs from the river bottom.

I am a flying fox. My forest home is in Australia. Not many bats in the world are bigger than me. I eat sweet fruit. I eat flowers. I am a kangaroo. My desert home is in Australia. Two big legs are how I hop. My baby rides in a pouch.

I am a blue penguin. Australia’s seashore is my home. I dig sand holes. I lay my eggs in the holes. The sea is where I catch fish. I am a koala. Australia’s trees are my home. Only special leaves are my food.

I am a spiny anteater. Australia’s deserts are my home. Its forests are my home too. A scare makes me roll into a ball. Ants are my yummy food. I am a weaver ant. Trees in Australia are my home. My nest is made from leaves. I am yellow. My body is green.
I am a crocodile. I live in Australia’s waters. I swim in rivers. I swim in lakes. I even swim in the sea. Australia is the home of all these animals. Australia is my home too.
Ants live in many places. Your yard has ants in the grass. Your yard has ants in the dirt. Ants also live on trees. Ants also live in your home. Food was left on the floor. Ants swarm that food.
These parts are on an ant. The thorax is one part. The abdomen is one part. The antennae are parts. The head is one part. The jaws are parts. The eye is one part.
Here is a very big ant. Here is a very small ant. Some ants have large jaws. Those jaws are strong. They use the jaws to cut. They cut food with them. They use the jaws to fight.
Most ants build nests. Some nests are under the ground. The top of the ground holds other nests. In a nest, ants do different jobs. Only the queen ant lays the eggs.

Some worker ants care for eggs. Some worker ants care for baby ants. Some of the worker ants get food. At the nest, soldier ants guard. Ants can be amazing animals. You can watch ants at work. Watching them can be fun.

No person can have too much good luck. Certain items are linked to good luck by many people. People around the world hold many ideas. Those ideas point to the source of good luck. People in India think good luck comes with an elephant.
People in Ireland think good luck comes with a four-leaf clover. People in England think good luck comes with a horseshoe.
People in China think good luck comes with a red lantern. People in Africa think good luck comes with a crocodile tooth.
In the United States, some think good luck comes with a rabbit's foot. Around the world, some think good luck comes with a rainbow.
Around the world, some think good luck comes with a falling star. What is one item that means good luck to you?

Drawbridges were the first ones that moved. These bridges helped people defend castles. Someone could raise the bridges. Attackers had to stay away. Bridges that cross rivers can move now. Ships are able to pass by safely. Moving bridges come in many types.
Some bridges tilt so one side goes up. The open part is that one side. Two pieces tilt up on other bridges. The open spot is in the middle. Some bridges fold the way an accordion folds.
Turning the middle opens a path. The open space is on either side. Lifting the middle is another way. The rise goes straight up. It moves into the air.
The middle can drop on some bridges. Down it goes, under the water. Some of the bridges curl up. They curl until they are out of the way.
The tilt on these goes to the side. Room is made underneath the bridges. Big ships pass each bridge safely.
This book ends with a very strange animal. What animal do you think it is? Its feet are webbed. Webbed feet help it swim. Each toe has a short claw. Could it be a penguin?

No. It has no white belly. What is it if it is not a penguin? Its tail is long and flat. It moves through water with that tail. It lives in rivers. It lives in lakes. It lives in ponds. Could it be a beaver?
No. This animal does not gnaw on trees. What is it if it is not a beaver? The eggs it lays are small and round. Its wide bill helps it get food. Could it be a duck?
No. It does not quack. It has no feathers. What is it if it is not a duck? Thick, shiny fur covers it. A long, sleek body lets it swim fast. Could it be an otter?

No. It has no whiskers. What is it if it is not an otter? This animal is a platypus. Australia is its home. It eats worms. It eats insects. It eats shrimp. It eats crayfish. That is the strange animal.
Allie, Jo, and Chris are going to the zoo. They will record what they see. Allie says she will make a table. Jo will use tallies, and Chris will draw a graph.
Allie starts to make her table. She calls the table Animal Table. Allie starts her table for animals. This is the start of her table.
Jo marks her animal tally chart. The bear has two tally marks. The elephant has three tally marks. Jo marks the bear and the elephant.
Then the kids see four wolves. Chris draws his animal graph. The graph has wolf, bear, and elephant. Chris draws the animals on his graph.
Elephant has three marks on the chart. Bear has two marks on the chart. Wolf has four marks on the chart. Which group has the most animals?
How many animals are there in all? The animal table shows elephant three. The animal table shows bear two. Wolf is on the animal table.
The notes agree with the chart and the table. The animal graph shows elephant, bear, and wolf. The tally chart shows elephant, bear, and wolf. The table keeps elephant, bear, and wolf together.
Have you met an earthworm? Earthworms are small animals. They change the soil. The changes are big.

Many rings make the body, and each ring can bend and stretch. The head end has a mouth, the tail is the back end, and a saddle sits on the body. The worm stretches out and pulls in to move. Slime on the skin can trail across a log. Slime keeps worms cool and wet, and it lets them move through soil. Worms come together to make babies. A ball of slime dries into a cocoon, and baby worms come out.

Getting the worm out is work for a bird. The worm is strong in the hole. Earthworms build long tunnels. Those tunnels are underground. Heat does not reach worms in them. Sunlight does not reach them either. Hungry animals cannot find them. A leaf gets pulled down into a hole. They slip out during the night. They look for food then. Another name for them is night crawlers. They eat dead leaves. They eat dead plants.

Water gets to roots through tunnels. Air gets to roots through tunnels. Farmers love these earthworms. The soil gets space from worms. From that space, plants get needed things. Those things help them grow. Worm waste helps those plants. The plants grow big. The plants grow strong. A mole eats these worms. A shrew eats these worms. A toad eats these worms. Many animals love worms for a meal.
Its head pokes out of the hole. Earthworms are small. Their job is still big. Growing plants is the job they do.
A cockroach is an insect. Each insect has a head. Each insect has three body parts. Each insect has six legs. The cockroach has these parts too.

Cockroaches have basic needs. Other insects have them too. Food is a basic need. Water is a basic need. Air is a basic need. Air comes in through the sides. A cockroach can meet one basic need with no head. They breathe through their sides.
A cockroach does not have to eat each day. A cockroach with no head cannot eat. A cockroach does not have to drink each day. A cockroach with no head cannot drink.

The American cockroach can live 28 to 42 days. The Surinam cockroach can live 11 to 24 days. The German cockroach can live 8 to 12 days. They were without food. They were without water. They did have heads. They can go a while with no food. They can go a while with no water. They need food. They need water. They need to breathe. They cannot live if a need is not met.
The pests are few among cockroaches. Those pests are trouble for people. Many people see them only as pests. They can be amazing too. Life can go on with no head. Are they amazing or pests?

title: A Canyon You Can See from Space

pages.text: This canyon is so big that it can be seen from space. In 1919, it became a national park. It is 277 miles, or 446 kilometers, long. In some places it is more than a mile deep, or 1.6 kilometers. The canyon lies in Arizona, in the United States.

Theodore Roosevelt's work kept the canyon protected. A national park means land that is protected. California condors are giant birds living here. They came close to dying out. People caught the condors. After safe care, the birds could have babies. The canyon came from the Colorado River through erosion. Erosion means some ground wears away. The river ran over the earth for many years. That long flow left a canyon behind. Each day wears away soil, rock, and other materials. The canyon grows deeper from that daily wear.

Color stripes cross the canyon. Each stripe is a layer of sediment. New layers sat on top of older layers. Earth changes over time show in those layers. People give the bottom rocks an age of nearly two billion years. The Havasupai, Navajo, Hualapai, Hopi, Zuni, and Apache make homes here. Life now is not the same as for relatives long ago. Stories and traditions were handed down. Native people once lived in the canyon. Many native people live here still.

Americans came to the canyon in 1869. Native people helped them learn. Those Americans helped make area maps. Later the canyon became a national park. Today the canyon still has help from native people. The South Rim is very popular. All year, every day, that rim stays open. The North Rim faces it from across the canyon. It is much higher up. It gets more snow. It is open only in warmer months.

Many people come to the canyon each year. Mule riders travel down to the bottom. Glass is the material of the Skywalk bridge. The Skywalk reaches out over the canyon. Hikes bring some people to the bottom. Walks around the bottom can last for weeks. Waterfalls and pools are found down there.
Rafts carry some people on the Colorado River. This river runs a very long way. Other people take a walk by the rim. The rim offers them an amazing view.

Big horn sheep live under protection in the canyon. Many other animals share that protection. The canyon will stay protected for years to come. People who visit get a view like nothing else. A winter day is one more time to see it. It is a natural wonder.

Many shops in Turkey sell lanterns. Those lanterns are beautiful. Turkey is a special country. A Turkish girl is with her doll. There is a Turkish flag. Some dolls wear Turkish clothes. Children dance at a Turkish festival.

Most of Turkey lies in Asia. A small part lies in Europe. More than eighty-two million people live there. Turkey is one of only five countries with land on two continents. The sea borders Turkey on three sides. Fishing is important to Turkish people. A bridge leads to Istanbul. Istanbul is the biggest city in Turkey.

On a city street, children play. That street is in Turkey. A group of children pass rice fields. After school, two children walk toward home. Their town is a Turkish town. Life is different in each part of Turkey. Some people live in small villages. Turkey has at least fifty thousand villages. Many children stay in villages with their families.

Big cities are home to some people in Turkey. About fifteen million people live in Istanbul. Ankara is the capital of Turkey. Near the Black Sea, the mountains rise. The water is very clear at many beaches. Weather is different across Turkey. Some places are very cold. Other places stay warm and sunny.

Food in Turkey is famous. People there enjoy different foods. They eat bread with meat inside and flatbread with cheese or herbs. A yogurt dip and fried eggplant with tomato are eaten too. Bulgur is a wheat cereal. Kebab is grilled meat on a stick. A plate of small foods, hummus, and flatbread with chopped meat are also served. Black tea is a common drink in Turkey. Dessert is the best part of the meal. The soft candy has lots of colors and flavors. A baked treat of dough, nuts, and syrup is a popular dessert.

Different groups have lived in Turkey a long time. Very old caves lie under hot-air balloons. People once lived in those caves. This city held people thousands of years ago. There are old ruins. There are hot springs. You can go inside the Hagia Sophia. You can see ruins in Ephesus. Each year, millions travel to Turkey. They explore special places. They look at works of art. They learn the history of Turkey. They learn the ways of life.

Now you know a lot about Turkey. Do you see why Turkey is special? Children from a small village are part of it. An old theater is part of it too. So is the area outside the Hagia Sophia. Boys in a park are part of it. Ankara is the capital city. Turkish is the main language. Lira is the name of the money. The official name is Republic of Turkey. The land is 784,000 sq. km. That is the same as 303,000 sq. mi.

Rain falls onto a clear lake. The lake is named Lake Itasca. Rain mixes into the clear water. A long journey begins at this lake. The upper river is the first part. The lower river is the next part. The water has a long way to go.

The lake flows into a river. A child could wade across here. The mighty Mississippi River begins here. Many other rivers run into it. The water travels through ten of the fifty United States. It takes three months to reach the sea. That sea is the Gulf of Mexico.

The upper river has locks and dams. They raise or lower the water around the boats. This makes travel safe for boats. Dams hold water back so boats do not hit the bottom. Boats carry wheat and corn south. This grain helps feed the world. Ground corn pours onto a barge in Iowa. A boat pushes a barge on down the river.

The Missouri joins the Mississippi. From the west comes a big dirty river. It mixes with the clear water. The Mississippi grows wide. The water turns brown. The Ohio joins from the east. Illinois, Kentucky, and Missouri meet there. The lower river grows deep. The lower river grows wider.

Often the Mississippi floods. The floods make a mess. Rich soil is left behind. The lower river has big cities. New Orleans is one big city. New Orleans is in Louisiana. A 2012 picture shows the city.

Boats carry iron and steel. They carry rubber, paper, and wood. Some items turn and go back. Some things move farther south. River otters play upriver. In tall trees, bald eagles have nests. Pallid sturgeon come in from the Missouri. In the lower river, alligators swim. The lower water is warmer.

A photo from space shows where the river ends. That lake rain is now at the sea. Some of the water may return. It may fall as rain on the lake. Then the journey can start again. It can happen again too.
Washington, D.C. holds a memorial for Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. People call him Dr. King. The memorial is there so people remember him.

Who was this man named Dr. King? Why do people remember him? He said now is always the time to do right. Many people watched him speak. His speech told about equality. Young Martin Luther King Jr. is shown with his family. He is at the front, on the right. This is the child who grew up in the South. He was a child in the 1930s. Laws in the South were not fair then. Those laws were unfair to Black people.

Men take a drink from the water fountains. The mark on the fountains is Colored. That word is rude today. That word can be hurtful. Laws kept Black people separate from white people. White children went to their own schools. A different set of schools was for Black children. Black people had to sit in the back on city buses. White people got the front seats.

Dr. King speaks to a group of people. Unfair laws are the topic. He wished for a change to the unfair laws. Many people heard his talks on changing laws. He said hate will not be ended by hate. He said love is what will end hate. Peaceful ways were his choice for change. He said too much hate was in the world already.

Dr. King led the people on a march. Many people went with him. The march said no to unfair laws. He worked with many people on the laws. Together they got the laws changed. A handshake joined him and President Lyndon Johnson. That handshake was in 1964. A bill was signed by President Johnson. Unfair laws were changed by that bill. The laws changed during 1964. The new laws were fairer than the old ones. Unfair treatment for skin color is against the law.

Two Black girls go to one school. Once, only white children went to that school. Schools can now hold both Black children and white children. Bus seats are open to people of every color. The back seat on the bus was refused by Rosa Parks. Her act was in 1955. Her courage helped the old laws change. Dr. King waves to a crowd in Washington, D.C. The wave comes before an important speech. Free people were what he wanted. Fair laws for every person were his goal too. His dream was for every color of person to get along.

He said a small thing can be done in a great way. People visit his memorial in Washington, D.C. They remember him on that visit. Fair laws were part of the dream they remember. Free people were part of that dream too. They carry on the work he started.

A monarch butterfly goes through a life cycle. The cycle has four stages. The first stage is the egg. The next stage is the caterpillar. Then comes the pupa stage. The last stage is the adult butterfly.

A female monarch lays an egg on a leaf. Usually she lays just one egg on that leaf. A caterpillar grows inside the tiny egg. The egg hatches in three to twelve days. A young caterpillar comes out of the egg. If two eggs are on the leaf, the caterpillar eats the other egg first. Then it eats its own shell. Next it eats the leaf it is on. The hungry caterpillar eats all the time.

Sticky silk comes from the caterpillar. The silk holds the old skin in place. The caterpillar wiggles free of that skin. The body grows fast. Skin stays the same size. The old skin splits and peels off. Only milkweed leaves are food for it. Bright black and yellow mark the body. Those colors give animals a warning. An animal that eats the caterpillar will get sick. Under the old skin sits new skin. Shedding of the skin happens four to six times. This growth lasts two to four weeks.

A grown caterpillar hangs from a branch. The skin on its back splits open. The open skin looks like a zipper. One last shed happens then. Bright green is the color of the new skin. The pupa looks as green as a leaf. The green color hides it from other animals. The green skin becomes hard. The caterpillar has become a pupa. One to two weeks pass inside the shell.

The butterfly takes air into its body. That air makes the body bigger. Then the shell splits open. The butterfly climbs out of the shell. A butterfly is what it is now. The new wings are wet. It hangs while liquid goes into the wings. The wings unfold because of the liquid. Rest comes next for the new butterfly. Upside down is how it must hang. If it does not hang that way, it cannot fly.

Most monarch wings reach about 4 inches. From tip to tip, that is 10 cm. Three to four hours pass while it hangs. The sun dries the wet wings. Air dries the wet wings too. Plants make a sweet liquid. The name of that liquid is nectar. Monarchs drink the nectar. Sipping is done with a long tongue. A tube is the shape of the tongue. Flight is possible after the wings dry. The butterfly leaves to find food. A mate is what it searches for next.
A female can lay 400 to 500 eggs over her life. A monarch may live only two to six weeks. The female lays the eggs. Then the life cycle starts once more.
Smart thinking was part of Abigail Adams. She had many good ideas. Her painting is from 1795. Early years come first. Then comes a war with Great Britain. After the war comes next.

In 1744, Abigail was born. She never went to a school. From her mom, she learned to read. From her mom, she learned to write. She became the wife of John Adams. A farm was their home. Abigail kept the farm going. Paintings show Abigail and John together.

Abigail lived in Massachusetts. It was one of thirteen colonies. At that time there was no United States. Great Britain ruled the colonies. People there had to pay taxes to Great Britain. A stamp showed that the tax had been paid. Many people did not want to be part of Great Britain.

John met with other men. They talked about a break from Great Britain. John worked to help that break. John was away from home a lot. The family was in her care. She kept the farm running. A painting shows John in that meeting.

They wrote many letters. Her letters shared her ideas. Her ideas earned his respect. Ending slavery was her wish. She wanted girls in school. She wanted grown girls to vote. These ideas came before their time. She cared for hurt soldiers. She served them meals. In 1781, the colonies won the war. Their new country was the United States.

The first vice president was John. Later he became the second president. They lived in the White House. That house got its first president and First Lady. It was the President's House then. As First Lady, Abigail was smart. She shared her ideas with people. Not all people liked her ideas. She still told them.

A statue of Abigail stands in Boston. Boston is in Massachusetts. In 1818, Abigail died. Her ideas lived on after that year. Those ideas still help the United States. They make the country a better place.

Animals come in many kinds. The elk is in the deer family. Male elk have large antlers. The antlers are on their heads. Elk can swim well. Elk can run very fast. Giraffes have spots. Giraffes have long necks. Giraffes are very tall.

A long winter coat is on this camel. Camels can live a long time with no food. Camels can live a long time with no water. Foxes eat small animals. Foxes eat insects. Foxes eat fruits. Foxes eat eggs. Holes in the ground are homes for foxes. The dog family includes the fox.

On land, no animal is larger than an elephant. Long trunks are part of elephants. Grasslands are one home for elephants. Forests are another home for elephants. Thick fur covers snow leopards. The fur keeps snow leopards warm. Snow leopards live on mountains. Those mountains are cold.

Zebras come from the horse family. Zebras have white stripes. Zebras have black stripes. Zebras live in grasslands. Neck hair on a zebra stands straight up. Kangaroos eat grass. Kangaroos eat other plants. Strong back legs let a kangaroo hop. A pouch is on the great gray kangaroo.
A polar bear lives in a cold place. Seals are food for polar bears. Birds are food for polar bears. Fish are food for polar bears. Part of a polar bear's time is in the water.
These are elf owls. Many animals live in holes. People call those holes burrows. I wanted to learn more about the burrow animals.

I do this work with my teacher. My teacher gave me help with the learning. A computer is how I shared my learning. Come see the things I learned. A desert tortoise stays in a burrow. This hole is home to a tortoise. The hole is in a desert. Digging a burrow gets it away from the heat.

A goliath bird-eating spider is huge. The spider is the size of a dinner plate. Its burrow is a hiding place. This hole is home to a big spider. Eggs are laid in a little bag. The bag is taken along to find food. This hole belongs to Atlantic puffins. Most of the time, puffins stay at sea.

A puffin bill may have bright colors. Some people call puffins the clowns of the sea. A puffin feeds its chick. Puffins dig a burrow into a cliff. That burrow is their nest. The egg gets care from both parents. A naked mole rat pokes its head out of its burrow. This hole is home to naked mole rats. These rats live in the dark.

Long front teeth help the mole rat dig. The rats do their digging as a team. They make tunnels so they can find food. One animal digs at the dirt. Other animals move that dirt away. A Japanese giant salamander leaves its burrow. This water hole is home to a big salamander. Rivers and streams are where it lives. It hides through the whole day. At night it hunts for food.

A male salamander keeps the eggs safe. Inside the burrow, the eggs stay safe. A female lays many eggs. A wombat burrow can be very long. Three school buses in a row show the length. The burrow may match that length. A mother wombat looks out of the hole. Her baby looks out beside her. This hole is home to a wombat. Daytime is for sleep in the burrow. Outside at night, it finds food.
Snakes make homes in burrows too. Burrows are homes for still more animals. Learning about these animals is so fun. More burrow animals are still to come.
At the beach, sand castles may be something you have seen. Have you seen a sand castle like this one?

Sand play is paid work for some people. They are known as sand sculptors. Amazing sand castles are not their only work. These artists make statues. The statues are made out of sand. The statues look interesting.

Glue is often sprayed on a finished statue. The glue keeps the sand from falling. Some of the statues take days to make. A sand statue can last for months. Giant sand statues mean a lot of work. The first need is a big pile of sand.
Then the artists fill wooden walls with sand. They add water while the walls are filled. Next comes a jump onto the wet sand. The jumps pack the sand down. This packing step is called a pound-up.
At last, carving of the sand starts. Carving begins high on the sandpile. Tools are used to carve the sand. Hands are used to carve it too. The carved sand can look like real people.

Animals with teeth can be carved. Claws can be carved on the animals. Sand can even be shaped like a city. Around the world, these artists enter contests. China once had a huge sand sculpture. It was one of the biggest ever built. Over 30 sculptors worked on it. They spent 75 days on the work. It stood 73 feet tall. That height is 22 m.
Amazing statues of many kinds are made from sand. The beginning was the same for each one. Sand play was the way each one started.

Some animals have a bad smell. Some plants have a bad smell too. The smell helps them stay alive. Skunks spray to protect themselves. The spray also protects their babies. A Tasmanian devil smells bad at times. Danger is when its bad smell starts.

Striped polecats are much like skunks. Fear makes a polecat raise its tail. Then it sprays a stinky liquid. Like kangaroos, opossums have pouches. An opossum plays dead near enemies. Stinky green slime comes from it too. The slime keeps enemies back.

The corpse flower smells like a dead body. That bad smell brings flies close. It brings beetles close too. A lesser anteater has rough fur. The fur keeps ants off its body. It shoots stinky liquid at enemies. Wolverines are called nasty cats. They smell very bad. A wolverine makes stinky liquid. The smell keeps other animals away. It also pees on food it does not eat right away.

Two hair layers cover the musk oxen. The hair keeps them warm. They fight over mates. Stinky pee keeps others away. The stinkbird has wings. It does not fly much. This bird eats leaves. Tiny living things break the leaves down. That way of eating smells bad.

Millipede spray can itch. It can burn too. A millipede cannot run fast. It makes stinky liquid near enemies. The stinkpot smells bad when enemies come. A musk turtle may live forty years. It may live sixty years. A mink frog smells like rotten onions. A mother mink frog can lay many eggs. She can lay 4,000 eggs.

A vulture eats dead animals. Smelly stomach acid helps it eat. It throws up when enemies come close. The throw-up smells very bad. A beetle sprays hot stinky liquid. A pop comes as the spray shoots. The heat can kill some enemies.
A female bird sprays a dark liquid. The liquid has a bad smell. She sprays to keep the nest safe. Animals can smell bad. Plants can smell bad too. Stink helps them live.

title: A Busy City on Two Continents

pages.text: The city of Istanbul is busy. Bridges are many in this city. Into this big city sails a ship. Europe holds some parts of the city. Asia holds the other parts. The name of the city is Istanbul. The country is Turkey. Two continents meet at Istanbul. A continent is one huge piece of land on Earth. Just a few cities besides this one sit on two continents.

Istanbul sits right on the water. No city in Europe has a larger number of people. Istanbul is a city that matters. People from different places come together here. Byzas led a group of people to this area. Say his name like BY-zuhss. The group left the city of Megara. Say Megara like MEH-guh-ruh. Megara is found in Greece. A map places Europe on one side. The map places Asia on the other side. Africa is on the map as well. The Black Sea is on the map. The Sea of Marmara is on the map. The Aegean Sea is on the map. The Mediterranean Sea is on the map. Italy is on the map. Turkey is on the map too.

Constantine the Great ruled this city at one time. Mehmed the Second ruled it at a different time. Other names belonged to the city before. The name became Istanbul in 1930. Long ago, the name was Byzantium. Say Byzantium like bih-ZAN-tee-uhm. That old name honored a leader called Byzas. A later name was Constantinople. That name honored Constantine the Great. Under the ground sits a huge open space. Long ago, water filled the whole space. People put that water to many uses. Very old water tanks stand all over Istanbul. No other tank here is bigger.

The market is huge. Stone is what the market is made of. Few covered markets in the world are older than this one. The earliest parts went up in 1461. Further parts went up in later years. Shop after shop fills the market. Covered streets in the market number 61. Shops inside number more than 4,000. Every day, more than 250,000 people come to shop. The tower is old. It stands on a small island. Time after time, the tower was torn down. Time after time, people built it once more. Watching ships was its first job. Later the lights gave help to ships. People eat at the tower now.

This tall tower went up in 1348. Over the years, people used the tower in many different ways. Today, people climb stairs on the inside. They look out over the city. When builders finished it, Istanbul had no taller building. This palace goes far back in time. Ruler after ruler lived inside it. The families of those rulers lived there too. That was long ago. High walls wrap the outside of the palace. These days the palace serves as a museum.

The museum roof is a huge dome. That dome is a round shape. People first raised the building to be a church. In a later age it turned into a mosque. After the mosque years, it was a museum. In our time, it is a mosque once again. This city square dates from the 1700s. Shops now line the square. Places to eat now line it too. Tall figures stand in the open square. The birth of Turkey is what those tall figures honor.

A high stone wall circles the city's oldest part. That oldest part stays inside the wall. Great places to see fill Istanbul. Every place holds a story of its own. A visit there feels like earlier days. It feels like time turned back. The wall is built of stone. The wall stands high. Stories wait in each great place. A visit brings the past up close.
Traci and Matthew play the Shape Game. They will build a tower with shapes. They will see if the tower stands or falls.
First, they will choose cards from a deck. Then, they will match the cards to real shapes. Last, they will use the shapes to build a tower.
Traci has a square. Matthew has a cube.
Traci has a circle. Matthew has a cylinder.
Traci has a triangle. Matthew has a pyramid.
Traci has a rectangle. Matthew has a box.
Traci has a cone. Matthew has a sphere.
Matthew and Traci have many shapes. They are ready to build a tower. They build a tower from many shapes. Will the tower fall or stand?
Could you use all of the shapes to build a tower? Is there a shape that you would not use?

title: A Gentle Giant of the Sea

pages.text: No fish is bigger than the whale shark. An adult's length matches a school bus. Length can reach 40 feet. That measure is 12.2 m. Weight can reach 40,000 pounds. That measure is 18,144 kg. A person might stand 6 feet tall. That measure is 1.8 m. A person might weigh 175 pounds. That measure is 79.4 kg.

Leave whale sharks alone when you are in the water. Do not touch them. Do not bother them. People still swim beside these fish. People still dive beside them. Gentle is how these fish act. They bring no danger to people. The head is wide. The head is flat. A huge mouth sits on the front. Often the mouth stays open during a swim.

Spots and stripes form a pattern on each whale shark. No two patterns are the same. The back is a dark color with light spots and light stripes. The belly is white. The skin is thick, and the scales are sharp. They travel at only 3 miles per hour. That measure is 5 kmph. Swimming uses the whole body. Other sharks swim mainly with the tail and the back end. A big fin rises on the back, and the tail fin is big too. Each side has five large gill slits. The mouth is at the front of the head. Other sharks have the mouth under the nose. The skeleton is cartilage, not bone. All sharks have this kind of skeleton.

Other fish sometimes swim along with them. Warm oceans in many parts of the world are home for them. They swim in the middle of the ocean and also near the shore. Staying at the surface is common. Very deep dives happen too. A map shows where they live and travel. It marks Europe, North America, Asia, Africa, South America, and Australia. It also marks the Equator and the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. A few whale sharks travel very far. Nobody is sure why those trips happen. Now and then they meet in a big group. A meeting of that size is rare.

Food for them includes tiny ocean animals. Tiny ocean plants are food too. They eat small fish. They eat squid. They eat fish eggs. Now and then a bigger fish is eaten. Chewing is not part of the meal. Water flows in the open mouth. The water brings food with it. Pads by the throat catch that food. Afterward the water flows away. They suck water in when they want lots of food.

Two swimmers float near a young whale shark. They are in the Sea of Cortez. These sharks are born as live babies. The babies are called pups. A pup looks like a small adult. Growth takes a long time. Life can last a long time too. One hundred years is a possible life span. A full-grown shark may reach twenty-five times a newborn's length.
People can swim near whale sharks. They are safe to be near. They are a special kind of fish. They are huge. They are also very gentle. Earth has no fish that is larger.

title: A Quiet Sport with a Club

pages.text: A golfer swings a club. The club hits a golf ball. Golf is a quiet sport. Golf is a fun sport. Players must be calm. Calm players can play well. Players must practice. Practice helps them get good.

A tee often holds the ball before the hit. The club hits the small ball. The ball is hard. The aim is a small hole. That hole sits in the ground. The winner uses the fewest hits. The ball has to go in the hole. A flagstick shows where the hole is. One area is the putting green. Green is its short name. The fringe is longer grass. It goes around the green. The fairway is one part. The teeing ground is another part. The rough has trees. The rough has shrubs. The rough has long grass. Sand fills a sand trap. The trap is a hole in the ground. A stream can be a water trap. A pond can be a water trap.

A hard swing sends the ball away. The green is where it should go. It may take several hits. The hole may take more than one hit. One hit can be enough for a lucky player. The ball goes in the hole on that hit. Sand fills some traps by the holes. A pond can trap the ball too. Rough grass grows on parts of a course. Sand traps can be there. Water traps can be there. More hits may be needed to get the ball out.

Each kind of shot has its own club. A far hit needs one kind. A short shot needs another kind. Play on a hole begins at one end. The other end has the green. The small hole is there. Nine holes can make a course. Eighteen holes can make a course. Each hole has a red flag on it. The course shown has nine holes. Tee areas on it run from one to nine.

Golf began hundreds of years ago. The first balls were made of wood. A photo shows an old golf ball and golf clubs. Balls are made of rubber and plastic now. New balls fly higher than old ones. New balls fly farther than old ones. Many people around the world love to play. The sport is popular in countries where people speak English. A list also names ten countries known for golf. The names are the United States and the United Kingdom. The names include Japan and Canada. They include Australia and Germany. They include France and China. They include Sweden and South Africa. The list is not a race score. It simply names those countries. The United States has more places to play golf than any other country. A map marks the Atlantic Ocean. It marks the Pacific Ocean. It marks the Indian Ocean.

Each year brings some big golf contests. Many people show up to watch. Some players enter the big events. One event can hold many contests. This can happen in a single year. Men play in one group of events. Women play in another group of events. Jack Nicklaus played better than every other golfer. Patty Berg is great at this game. Tiger Woods is great at this game too.

Funny moments happen on the course. An animal may get very close. Geese share one course with the players. California is where that course is. Elk eat grass on the courses. Colorado is where those courses are. Would you like to try this game? Hard practice can make it fun.

Fireworks glow behind the Washington Monument. The fireworks are colorful. George Washington helped the United States. He helped the country win freedom. That freedom was from the British. People call him a hero for this. Builders made it to honor George Washington. He was the first president. His country was the United States. The monument is a tall white pillar.

Washington, D.C. is where it stands. It stands in the National Mall. The National Mall is a grassy area. The area is public. That city has no taller building. A law says other buildings must stay shorter. Even many miles away, it stays in sight. The Lincoln Memorial stands nearby. The Potomac River is nearby. The Korean War Veterans Memorial is nearby. The Vietnam Veterans Memorial is nearby. The Reflecting Pool is nearby. The Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial is nearby. Constitution Gardens is nearby. The World War II Memorial is nearby. The Tidal Basin is nearby. The Thomas Jefferson Memorial is nearby.

The height matches eight White Houses. Its height is 555 feet. That is 169 m. The height also matches twenty-nine giraffes. Builders used stone. In 1861, it stood only 150 feet tall. That was 45.7 m. The job started in 1848. Many times the job stopped. Many times the job started again.

At some times, money ran short. Inside the United States, a war stopped the work too. Doors first opened in 1885. Workers finished the very top. People climbed 898 steps to reach the top. A statue of George Washington is inside. That same statue once stood in the Lincoln Memorial. A visit can take you inside. A museum fills part of the inside.

Special stones cover the inside walls. U.S. states gave some of the stones. Other stones came from people. Those people wanted the monument built. A stone from New York State shows a Latin word. The word means higher. Some stones came from outside the United States. Wales gave one of those stones. Posters inside show the sights. Each side has two small windows. Visitors can go up to the top. From the top they see Washington, D.C.

Fifty U.S. flags stand around the monument. All fifty states have a flag here. A large stone sits at a corner. Many things rest inside that stone. George Washington receives honor from those things. The United States receives honor from them too. The flags stay up through the day. The flags stay up through the night. The 2011 earthquake damaged the monument. More damage came from a storm after that. Fixing it took almost three years. After the earthquake, workers looked for cracks. The cracks were in the stone blocks.
The grass nearby is a fine place to fly kites. The grass is also a fine place for picnics. Each year, many people come to this monument. What would you hope to see there?

A map shows Mount Desert Island. Maine is on that map. Canada is on that map. The coast of Acadia meets the sunrise. No state sees the Sun rise before Maine. The park is in Maine. Acadia National Park is one Maine place for that early Sun. People go there to see the Sun early.

Each year millions visit Acadia. Sunrise on tall peaks draws them. Islands draw them. Forests draw them. Lakes draw them. The rocky coast draws them. Water adds beauty. Rocks add beauty. Trees add beauty. A child gives an Acadia tide pool a close look. In one pool, a starfish rests. Colorful seaweed rests in a pool too. Beaches hold tide pools after the tide goes out. Many living things live in those pools.

Acadia is a great place to watch birds. Some fly over as they head south. Other birds live in the park all year. People have seen hundreds of kinds of birds there. A scientist puts a metal band on a chick, the smallest falcon in Acadia. The band helps scientists study the chick as it grows. They can also see where it goes. Peregrine falcons are one of the fastest animals on Earth. Human actions killed many of the birds. Acadia worked hard to bring them back. Now falcon chicks are born in the park every year.

Many mammals have a home in Acadia. Some mammals use both water and land. The beaver lives in the park. The mink lives in the park. The porcupine lives in the park. Baby foxes live in the park. Some mammals live in the forest.

Some of those mammals live in the ground. The mole lives in the ground. The groundhog lives in the ground. The Wabanaki are Native people. They first lived in and around Acadia. They still live in Northern Maine and parts of Canada today. Some build canoes and baskets like those who came before them. Some guide visitors or sell fish. Some also teach people at the yearly Native American Festival. Wabanaki people use trees in their area to make canoes. Native people protected this land for years. Then Maine became a state. Rich people bought land along its coast. Soon, many different people owned bits of the area.

Some of those people wanted to protect the area. They donated the land to the government. In 1919, that land became a national park. George Dorr lived alone on Mount Desert Island. Over time, he bought lots of land. Then he donated it. He had spent all his money by the time he died in 1944. But Dorr had made his dream come true. Acadia had become a national park. It is still growing today, piece by piece. A photograph shows George Dorr looking out over the park he helped create. President Barack Obama and his family hiked in Acadia National Park in 2010. There is plenty to see and do in Acadia. Some people come to hike, climb, fish, or ride a bicycle.

Cadillac Mountain is a sunrise place. Visitors look out from Cadillac Mountain. They watch the Sun come up from it. Make the trip if a chance comes your way. The trip shows you the early Sun. The trip shows you land meeting sea. Acadia has both of those sights.

title: Air In and Out of My Lungs

pages.text: My lungs sit inside a body system. That system keeps me alive. My body needs oxygen. Oxygen has to come in through my lungs. I breathe air. The oxygen is in that air. Air is where the oxygen comes from. With each breath, my lungs pull the oxygen in. My lungs do that pulling.

Each new breath starts at the nose or the mouth. The air gets warm in the nose and throat. The air gets clean there too. Tiny hairs do that cleaning. Those hairs are in the nose and the throat. Next the air moves down the throat. It goes into both lungs. Inside, tubes carry the air. The tubes split like the branches of trees.

Tiny sacs wait at the end of the tubes. Bunches of grapes are what the sacs look like. Balloons are another way to see the sacs. A trade happens inside the balloons. Oxygen is one part of the trade. Carbon dioxide is the other part. My lungs make the trade there. The tiny balloons are the trade spot.

This waste air is carbon dioxide. My body has no use for it. My blood carries it on the trip to my lungs. In the tiny balloons, the blood lets the carbon dioxide go. The blood takes oxygen next. The blood carries that oxygen all through me. Every breath runs the trade one more time.

Breathing in sends my chest outward. Room opens up in my body for the lungs. The room lets my lungs fill. They fill with oxygen. Breathing out brings my chest back in. The lungs let carbon dioxide leave. Waste air leaves when the chest comes in.

Breathing goes on all the time. No thought is needed for this breathing. If I had to think about each one, nothing else would fit. While I rest, about 24 breaths come each minute. An hour adds up to more than 1,400 breaths. Resting is the time for that minute count.

I feel thankful for my lungs. They work very hard for me. They work in the system that lets me stay alive. They pull in oxygen on every breath. They let carbon dioxide back out. They keep the trade going all the time. More than 1,400 breaths fill one hour.
Many kinds of beaches are found around the world. Some of them surprise people. Some of them seem amazing.

New Zealand has a place called Hot Water Beach. Visitors there dig holes into the sand. The holes are not for sand castles. The goal is to sit in water that is warm. That warm water rises from beneath the sand. California has a place called Glass Beach. For years, glass trash was dumped into the ocean there. Waves wore the glass smooth. Rocks wore the glass smooth too. The smooth glass looks like gems now.

A beach does not have to sit on the shore. Spain has one with land all the way around it. Underground tunnels let the water reach that beach. Japan has a place called Tiny Star Beach. Sand grains there have the shape of tiny stars. The grains are shells, not plain sand. Time wore the shells into those star shapes.

California has a place called Bowling Ball Beach. Round rocks there look just like bowling balls. Low tide is when you can go see them. Hawaii has a place called Black Sand Beach. Rare turtles visit this beach of black sand. The black color comes from volcano rock. The rock is broken into tiny pieces.

Bermuda has a place called Pink Sand Beach. Cotton candy is the same color as this sand. White sand is part of the mix. Pieces of red shell are part of the mix. The mix is what makes the sand pink. South Africa has a place called Giant Rock Beach. Giant rocks cover the beach. People come to visit. This beach is home to about three thousand penguins.

Australia has a place called White Sand Beach. Maybe you have walked on white sand before. This beach holds the record as the whitest in the world. Australia also has 75 Mile Beach. Planes can use this very long beach as a runway. Swimmers here should take care. Sharks fill the water.

Hawaii is home to one of these beaches. Beach sand may be white. It may be black. It may be red. It may even be green. A few amazing beaches look like other planets. Which beach would you want to see?
A brother can be the same age as you. A sister can be the same age too. They can even look the same. This can happen when they are twins.

Twins grow in their mother at the same time. They can be two brothers. They can be two sisters. They can be a brother and a sister. Mothers are more likely to have twins today. Twins are more common in some families. Identical twins may like the same food. They may like the same clothes. They must be two girls or two boys. It can be hard to tell them apart. Some can change places. No one can tell them apart!

About one in four identical sets are mirror twins. Face to face, they look like a mirror. A freckle may sit on opposite sides. A hair part may sit on opposite sides. Fingerprints are patterns on your fingertips. The twins may look very alike. Their fingerprints never match. They may like the same things. They may like different things. Same interests may keep them together.

Fraternal twins are more common than identical twins. The most common pair is a boy and a girl. These twins can be two boys. They can be two girls. They can be a girl and a boy. They are like regular brothers or sisters. Their birth came at the same time.

Fraternal twins often enjoy different things as they grow. Different actions are more common for them. The same actions can happen too. Growing up together can lead to that. Twins have a bond as babies. They do everything together then. A special bond is common. Sharing a mother's body may start that bond.

After birth, twins like to stay close. They may make up their own words. The words are for talking to each other. When they learn to talk, made-up words usually stop. Many twins go to Twinsburg, Ohio, each summer. Most dress identically for the day. The day they celebrate is Twins Day. Each year, no twin gathering in the world is bigger than Twins Day. An almost exact look is possible for identical twins. Fraternal twins usually show a different look. Just some twins look almost exactly alike. Just some twins act almost exactly alike. Some twins like matching things. Some twins do not like matching things. A very different look can happen. A very different way of acting can happen.
Twins are not one person split in two. Each twin is one of a kind.

Get one piece of printer paper. Hold it so the paper is tall. Now make the first fold. Use one third of the paper. Bring that third down. The folded third lies on the sheet. A third is the amount in this fold. Down is the direction of the fold.

Next, find a corner on the folded part. Use the top left corner. Fold it in toward the center. A triangle forms from that fold. The top right corner gets the same fold. That corner folds toward the center too. Another triangle forms. These folds begin the nose. The nose is the front of the airplane.

Next, fold the top of the paper down over the triangle. Let that fold pass the bottom of the triangle by about a finger's width. The extra strip is the overlap. Fold that overlap back under the bottom edge. This tuck helps keep the nose in place.

Now bring the two sides of the paper together. Point the triangle toward the inside. The triangle is on the inside. The slanted edges should meet. The match of the edges should be even. Wings come from these slanted edges. Open the left side out into a wing. The dashed line shows where to press. Press the left wing fold flat.

Now match the left wing with the right wing. Fold the right wing out. Press that wing down. A top view shows the paper from above. A front view shows the paper from the front. Then fold the outer edge of each wing up. The fold is about a finger's width. Press down on each edge fold.

A top view shows the next folds. A front view shows them too. Unfold the wing edges. The edges should point straight up. A straight flight gets help from those edges. The wings need to rise off the body. Raise both wings to the same height. The two wings should match in height.

The paper airplane is done. You folded it from printer paper. The nose is at the front. Both wings sit at one height. The wing edges stay up. A finger's width shaped two folds. The dashed line guided a wing fold. Then let the new plane go into the air.

title: A Day at the Art Museum

pages.text: An art museum visit is set for my sister and me. It is called the Getty Museum. Los Angeles is the city where it stands. Our ride there is by shuttle. The window lets us see the museum. The building is a work of art too.

This museum is drawn out on a map. The map shows where the shows are. The map shows what each show holds. The map helps us pick what to see. A special show is happening. Very old art is in that show. The art comes from two cities in Italy. A volcano buried one of the cities. The show looks exciting.

A very big painting hangs here. Light falls on the dress of the woman. She looks as if she sits right here. A wall note gives the story of the artist. The story of the painting is in that note too. A very old sculpture stands here. Some parts of the sculpture broke off. How the man looked is still clear. Could this man have been a king?

I like this painting. From above, the little girl seems to see us. She seems surprised that we are here. Beauty shows in these old paintings. The collar of the lady has tiny lines. Her dress has tiny lines too. A brush of very tiny size was in the hand of the artist.

Snack time has come. A snack bar is part of the museum. Food is sold there. Drinks are sold there too. My sister is eating lunch. A costume room is her favorite part. She puts on a costume. She looks like a person in an old painting. Someone takes her picture after that.

We can make art on our own. Special benches are there for drawing. We take pencils and paper. We draw the flowers with them. People call a flower picture a still life. The museum has more paintings than it can show. Some paintings are stored away. A computer shows the stored ones. A note about each painting is on the computer. A note about each artist is on it too.

A gift shop is inside the museum. Lots of books about art are here. Books for kids are here too. I see art that is really colorful. I see art that is crazy. This book is one I would like. My sister and I feel tired. Fun was still part of the day. A visit here is a great one. I hope a new visit comes soon.

People can see the Statue of Liberty today. The statue stands very tall. No statue in the United States is taller than this one. People can see it from far away. It is a very big statue. How did a statue this big come to be? A statue is a kind of art. It may be shaped like a person. It may be shaped like an animal. Liberty means you may have your own beliefs.

A man in France had an idea in 1865. His name was Edouard de Laboulaye. Help for the United States was his aim. He wanted that help for the 100th birthday. He said a gift should come from France. The United States would receive the gift. He picked the Statue of Liberty as that gift. France and the United States chose a place. They chose an island near New York City. The island is named Liberty Island. Water goes all the way around an island.

The United States made the base. France made the statue. The statue had to look good. It also had to last a long time. The inside part is iron. The outside part is copper. Builders worked in Paris, France. In 1883 a piece sat in a workshop there. In 1884 the finished statue stood in Paris. Workers joined the parts. Moving it as one whole piece was impossible. They separated the parts again. A big ship carried the parts. That ship went to the United States.

All the work was done in 1886. A big celebration took place that year. The president of the United States spoke that day. A painting shows that day. Workers fixed the statue in 1985. Today people see a large woman colored green. Its weight is equal to 115 cars. With the base, it stands as tall as a building of 30 stories.

The copper shows many colors. At the start, the color matched a new penny. The air changed the copper as years went by. Green became the color. This statue is a work of art. Friendship is another thing this statue stands for. It has welcomed many people. Those people moved to the United States. Children waved hello. They were greeting a new home. That home was the United States.

The statue carries a special meaning. The right hand holds a torch. The torch stands for freedom. The left hand holds a tablet. July 4, 1776 is written on that tablet. Ancient Roman numbers show the date. That day the United States became a country of its own. Each year, visitors come from every part of the world.

A girl comes to see the Statue of Liberty. People ride out to look at it. They come because the statue means freedom. Big boats bring visitors to the statue. The boats take the visitors back too. A tablet is a flat surface for writing. A torch is a stick with fuel at one end. The fuel can burn. Burning fuel gives off light. Freedom means you may act as you wish. It also means you may think as you wish. Liberty means you may act as you wish too.

Brazil is the largest country in South America. Almost half of that continent is inside its borders. A map shows the land around it. Guyana is on the map. Venezuela is on the map. Suriname is on the map. French Guiana is on the map. Colombia is on the map. Peru is on the map. Bolivia is on the map. Paraguay is on the map. Argentina is on the map. Uruguay is on the map. São Paulo is on the map. Rio de Janeiro is on the map. São Luis is on the map. Brasília is on the map. The Atlantic Ocean is on the map. The Pacific Ocean is on the map. North America is on the map.

Other countries border Brazil on the north. Other countries border it on the south. Other countries border it on the west. The Atlantic Ocean lies to the east. Brasília is the capital city. Brasília is said bruh-ZIL-yuh. The city became the capital in 1960. The city was built to be the capital. The city was built in only a few years. New buildings fill Brasília. Soccer is the most popular sport in Brazil. People call soccer futebol. Futebol is said FOOT-bohl. Brazil's people number more than two hundred million. Most people there speak Portuguese. Portuguese is said POR-chuh-geez.

Cities are home to most people there. Many of those cities are on the coast. Some people live out in the country. São Paulo is the largest city. São Paulo is said SOW POW-low. Brazil has many different kinds of land. The land has beaches. The land has tall mountains. The land has flat places covered with water. The Guiana Highlands are one area. The Amazon River is one area. The Amazon Basin is one area. The Brazilian Highlands are one area. The Pantanal Wetlands are one area. The Coastal Lowlands are one area.

The Amazon rainforest grows in Brazil. Nearly half the country is this forest. It is the biggest rainforest in the world. The Amazon River runs through that rainforest. It is one of the longest rivers in the world. Rio de Janeiro holds one of the largest Carnaval celebrations. The first sound is REE-oh. The rest sounds like DAY zhuh-NAIR-oh. Carnaval comes during Brazil's summer. The holiday goes on for four days.

People dress up for Carnaval. They walk in big parades. They play many kinds of music. Few parties anywhere are bigger than this one. People dance special dances then. Sloths live in the Amazon rainforest. A red tree frog lives there. Other frogs live there too. Parrots live there too. Parrot feathers are colorful. Some colorful frogs live on the ground. Some colorful frogs live in the trees.

The rainforest is full of ants. Fire ants live in that forest. Leaf-cutter ants live in that forest. Leaf-cutter ants can cut very large leaf pieces. They can carry those large pieces. Spiders are common in that forest. The biggest spider in the world lives there. That big spider can eat birds. A large statue stands near Rio de Janeiro. The statue is Brazil's most famous landmark. Brazil is an exciting country. It has big cities. Its forests hold many animals. Which part of Brazil do you like most?
The population is 211,049,527. The land covers 8,458,417 sq km. The same land is 3,265,813 sq mi. The currency is the real. Real is said ray-AHL. These figures come from 2019.

Egypt lies in North Africa. The Mediterranean Sea is to the north. The first part of the sea name is MEH-duh-tuh. The last part is RAY-nee-uhn. East of Egypt is the Red Sea. Other countries lie to the west. Other countries lie to the south. Israel is on the map. Alexandria is on the map. Cairo is on the map. Jordan is on the map. The Giza Pyramids are on the map. Saudi Arabia is on the map. Libya is on the map. The Gulf of Suez is on the map. Luxor is on the map. The Aswan High Dam is on the map. Aswan is on the map. Sudan is on the map. Europe is on the map. Asia is on the map. Africa is on the map.

The Cairo Opera House stands in Cairo. Along the Nile in Cairo, the buildings look modern. Cairo is the capital city. Cairo is said KEYE-roh. Africa has few cities larger than this one. Cairo's people number above twenty-one million. Camels help some people do their work. The land for that work is hot. The land for that work is dry. Egypt is home to more than 106 million people. Most of the people speak Arabic. Farming towns are home to many people. Those towns are along the Nile River.

Farming is good on both sides of the Nile. Some farmers grow cotton along the river. Clothes are made from that cotton. Farmers grow rice. Farmers grow wheat. Farmers grow other foods too. Desert land covers every part of Egypt. In the east, you find the Nile River. It is longer than every other river. The Libyan Plateau is on the land map. The Sinai Peninsula is on the land map. The Qattara Depression is on the land map. The Sinai Desert is on the land map. Mount Catherine is on the land map. The Sahara Desert is on the land map. The Eastern Desert is on the land map. The Western Desert is on the land map. Lake Nasser is on the land map. The Gulf of Suez is on the land map.

Many towns sit along the Nile. It also runs through many cities. The river ends at the Mediterranean Sea. The land at that end is the Nile Delta. Those Sinai peaks stand very tall. Sinai is said SEYE-neye. Egypt has other mountains too. The east has tall mountains. The west has low mountains.

The ibex is a type of goat. The ibex lives in the desert. Ibex is said EYE-beks. The fennec fox lives in the desert. The spiny-tailed lizard lives in the desert. Lizards live in those deserts. Other animals live in the deserts. Some people raise water buffalo. Some people raise sheep. Some people raise goats. Some people use camels to travel from place to place. Artists painted gods on tomb walls. Artists painted gods on temple walls. Egypt is a very old land. Long ago, kings called pharaohs ruled. Pharaohs is said FEHR-ohz. Some people believed those kings were gods.

The Pyramids of Giza are some of the tombs. Giza is said GEE-zuh. A gold mask is one old treasure. The pharaohs had huge pyramids built. Pyramids is said PIHR-uh-midz. These buildings are tombs for the pharaohs. Gold treasures were placed inside the tombs. Some treasures are kept in museums now. Egypt gets many visitors every year. Egypt is an amazing country. Egypt is a very old country too. There is much that is important to learn here.
The population is 106,156,692. The land covers 995,450 sq km. The same land is 622,272 sq mi. The capital city is Cairo. The primary language is Arabic. The currency is the Egyptian pound.

Mexico sits in North America. The United States is on the north side. Central America is on the south side. Sea water lies to the east. Sea water lies to the west. The Pacific Ocean is the western sea. The Gulf of Mexico is the eastern sea. The Gulf of California is on the map. The Baja Peninsula is on the map. The Yucatán Peninsula is on the map. Mexico City is on the map. Belize is on the map. Guatemala is on the map. Honduras is on the map. El Salvador is on the map. South America is on the map.

Old buildings stand in lots of Mexican cities. Many cities in Mexico have new buildings. Mexico is home to more than 120 million people. Most of the people live in cities. Mountains surround Mexico City. Two of those mountains are volcanoes. Mexico City is the capital. It is one of the oldest cities in North America. More people live there than in any other city in North America!

Some Native peoples speak their own languages. Spanish is the language most people speak. Mexico has more Spanish speakers than any other place. Mountains cover much of the country. Canyons cover much of the country. The Sonoran Desert lies in the north. The Chihuahuan Desert lies in the north. Those northern deserts are dry. Copper Canyon is part of the land. The south is covered with forests. The Mexican Plateau is one land area. The Sierra Madre Oriental Mountains are here. The Sierra Madre del Sur Mountains are here. Pico de Orizaba is here. A pair of land pieces reaches into the sea. Baja is like a long finger. Baja is said BAH-hah. Yucatán is more like a thumb. Yucatán is said yoo-kah-TAHN.

Mountain lions roam the deserts. Many different animals live in Mexico. Hot wet forests are home to parrots. Frogs live in those forests. Plenty more animals share those forests. Hot dry deserts are home to foxes. Lizards live in those deserts. Other animals live in the deserts too. Day of the Dead toys include skulls. Day of the Dead toys include skeletons. Mexico marks many special days. This holiday goes on for three days. The days are a happy time. People remember their loved ones. They light candles. They wear masks.

People remember a day from long ago. On that day Mexico began a fight. The fight was to be free. People dress up on the holiday. People walk in parades. People light fireworks. The fireworks belong to Independence Day. Corn is used to make tortillas. Tortillas is said tohr-TEE-uhz. In Mexico, corn matters at meal time. Corn is part of almost every meal. People eat pieces of cactus. People eat chicken. People eat pork. Some meals come out of the sea.

Cooks in Mexico often use peppers. Some of the peppers are hot. Chile peppers are one hot kind. Chile is said CHIH-lee. Some peppers are not hot. Those peppers change how food tastes. Peppers are used in many dishes. Visitors come from all over the world. They come to see the beaches. Mexico is an exciting country. Many different people live there. Many different animals live there too. Which part of Mexico do you like most?

The population is 127,575,529. The land covers 1,964,375 sq km. The same land is 758,450 sq mi. The capital city is Mexico City. The primary language is Spanish. The currency is the peso. Peso is said PAY-soh.

In Argentina, a boy looks after his horse. Argentina is a country in South America. It ranks second in size there. It ranks eighth in size in the world. Its borders touch five other countries. Bolivia is one of those countries. Paraguay is one of those countries. Brazil is one of those countries. Chile is one of those countries. Uruguay is one of those countries. The Pacific Ocean lies on one side. The Atlantic Ocean lies on the other side. A map marks the city of Buenos Aires.

Argentina's population is about forty-three million. Buenos Aires is the capital city. The name means fair winds. That city holds about fifteen million people. It is the largest city in Argentina. Most people live in big cities. Country land is home for the others. Some of those people are farmers. The farmers grow wheat. The farmers grow grapes. Workers gather the wheat. Workers gather the grapes.

The people of Argentina come from lands everywhere. Many of them come from Europe. Most people there speak Spanish. Some people watch a parade. A market is where some people buy goods. Students in a class learn from their teacher. The land has mountains. The land has lakes. The land has rivers. The Andes Mountains stand in the west. They are the longest mountain group in the world. Mount Aconcagua stands in that group. The Paraná River crosses the land. The Iguazú River is there too.

Monkeys live in Argentina. Wild cats live in Argentina. Plenty of animals besides those also live there. Argentina has some lovely rivers. Some river water drops from very high places. Few waterfalls anywhere are larger than these. The waterfalls are very tall. A painting shows people at work. Their work is the effort to free the land from Spain. People have lived there for thousands of years. Spanish rule covered the country in earlier times. Then army leaders took control.

The army leaders set the rules. People had no say in those rules. Most people were treated in an unfair way. Today, people can help make the rules. They choose their leaders. The chosen leaders think as the people do. A woman votes in Argentina. People gather for a fireworks show. Days go by during one huge party. Some people come dressed as clowns. People dress up as animals. Music plays at the party. People dance at the party. A big parade goes through the streets. A colorful float rides in the parade.

Pies in Argentina can hold many fillings. Meat sits on a grill while a family cooks. Grilled meat is food that people eat. People also eat little pies. Some pies are filled with meat. Some pies are filled with vegetables. Some pies are filled with cheese. Night lights shine across Buenos Aires buildings. People from around the world live in this country. Their efforts keep the country a great place. They help give it a bright tomorrow.

The population is 43,646,358. The land covers 2,736,690 square kilometers. That area is 1,056,642 square miles. The capital city is Buenos Aires. The main language is Spanish. The main religion is Roman Catholic. The money is called the Argentine peso. A border is the line between countries. A capital is the city of the main offices. Control is the power to decide. Crops are plants that farmers grow for food. The Atlantic Ocean has Europe on its east side. Europe lies north of Africa. Wheat is a kind of grain. People grind wheat into flour. Flour goes into bread. Flour goes into pasta. Flour goes into many desserts.

One part is Introduction. One part is Archerfish. One part is Trap-Door Spider. One part is Beaver. One part is Chameleon. One part is Flying Dragon. One part is Leaf Insect. One part is Leaf-Rolling Weevil. One part is Praying Mantis. One part is Mole. One part is Sea Dragon. One part is Conclusion. One part is Glossary.
