The North Pole and the South Pole are the points farthest north and south on me along my axis. Seasons are the four periods of a year. Tilted means slanted, not straight.

A painting from the 1670s shows a woman pulling lice from a young boy. Head lice have bothered people for thousands of years. Many people do not know what they are or where they come from. Some people think lice are a sign of a filthy home. Others think only people who do not wash enough get them.

One insect is a louse, but two or more are lice. Getting lice is not about a clean home, washing, or hair length. They affect kids and adults, rich and poor, all over the world. Head lice look like body lice, but they are a bit smaller. An adult head louse is about the size of a pencil point.

Their small size makes them hard to spot and hard to catch. Strong claws help lice hold tight to human hair. The claws cannot help a louse jump. Head lice usually spread when people touch heads. Sometimes a louse rides on a shared hat, comb, or other item.

Cats and dogs can get lice, but not the human kind. People and pets cannot give lice to each other. A louse on a comb usually dies before reaching another person. Nits are tiny eggs that stick to hair with special glue. They must stay warm near the scalp in order to hatch.

Nits take seven to ten days to hatch. Young lice then pass through three growing stages. They must feed within twenty-four hours, or they die. They become adults in about ten to twelve days. Bites do not hurt, but saliva makes them red and itchy.

The first sign is usually a ticklish feeling in your hair. They do not like light and can crawl quickly to avoid it. A lice comb has fine teeth that remove lice and nits. Hot air can kill lice and nits without chemicals. Students at the University of Utah tried a hot-air machine.

Super lice are harder to kill than other head lice. Chemicals that worked in the past no longer kill them. Some people use olive oil for weeks and sleep in a shower cap. Lice do not mean dirty hair or a dirty house. Anyone can get them, so spread the word, not the lice!

William Shakespeare was a poet and a playwright in England. He was born in 1564 and died in 1616. People have loved his exciting plays for more than four hundred years. People feel happy, sad, shocked, or scared, and they think about good and evil. A painting may show Shakespeare, but experts are not sure.

William was born to John and Mary Shakespeare in April 1564. He probably went to a very good school as a boy. Most people then did not know how to read or write. He married Anne in 1582, and they had three children. By 1592 he acted in London, and in 1599 he helped found a theater.

Theater was exciting, with fancy costumes and sword fights. Crowds booed bad guys, cheered good guys, and threw food. Most plays were in afternoon daylight, and only men could act. Shakespeare wrote tragedies, histories, and comedies. Tragedies are sad plays about people who make mistakes.

Students in California and actors in England act in Henry V. That play is about one of England's kings. His history plays are mostly about kings of England. His comedies are often funny love stories. For hundreds of years, people have laughed, cried, and loved his stories.

Students in Denver, Colorado, act, and people watch outdoors in Canada. People relate to love, hate, bravery, and power, now or long ago. Iago from Othello is evil yet human, and Romeo and Juliet shows true love. People read his plays in their own language, and festivals draw large crowds. Children act in his plays, and many plays have been made into films.

Shakespeare wrote one hundred fifty-four sonnets about love. A sonnet is a special poem with fourteen lines. His most famous sonnet compares someone to a summer day. He invented words like buzzer, gloomy, hint, eyeball, and leapfrog. He died in 1616, and a friend said his work was for all time.

Today Shakespeare is thought to be one of the greatest writers ever. His exciting plays touch people and show how hard and beautiful life is. He was born in Stratford and married Anne Hathaway in 1582. Susanna was born in 1583, and twins Hamnet and Judith in 1585. The Globe Theatre opened in 1599, and his plays were published in 1623.
